critical_code_review_comments: seeder.py:490 — the log line `log.info('Running seeds… (PROD_MODE=%s)', settings.PROD_MODE)` prints the boolean to server logs on every startup. That is not a credential leak but it does write PROD_MODE state to log aggregators. If /api/health deliberately omits this flag (SEC-004(d) at server.py:177-180), the parallel decision to log it plaintext during boot is slightly inconsistent. Non-blocking — startup logs are a different trust boundary than the public health probe.

seeder.py:478-535 — `run_seeds()` bifurcates on PROD_MODE inside the function body. When more branches (e.g., prod-safe admin invite bootstrap) get added later, this function will grow past readable size. Consider extracting `_run_prod_safe_seeds()` and `_run_preview_seeds()` helpers so the PROD_MODE gate is a 3-line dispatcher. Also, the returned dict shape differs between the two branches (`prod_mode_seed_skipped` key only appears in prod). The test at test_deploy_readiness_prod_mode_seed_guard.py:105 asserts `'prod_mode_seed_skipped' not in counts` for preview — that contract is fine, but downstream consumers of the dict (there is currently one: server.py:103 log line) should never .get() the key without a default.

internal_router.py:42-64 — the 503 refusal in prod mode is defensive-in-depth (belt + suspenders on top of the fact that the fixture user does not exist in prod). Good. However, the endpoint is still mounted unconditionally at server.py:213. Consider wrapping `app.include_router(fixture_internal_router)` in `if not settings.PROD_MODE:` so the OpenAPI schema in prod does not even advertise the route. Minor — the 503 already prevents any state mutation.

server.py:55-59 fail-fast: RuntimeError from module top-level fires cleanly under `python -c 'import server'` (verified). However under uvicorn/gunicorn workers this raises at import-time in each worker, which produces a fanout of stack traces in the process manager log. Consider moving the guard into the lifespan startup handler and calling `sys.exit(1)` so the message is emitted once. Non-blocking — the current behavior does fail-fast, just noisily.

test_deploy_readiness_prod_mode_seed_guard.py — nicely isolated (ephemeral Mongo db per test + sync pymongo teardown to avoid closing an already-closed asyncio loop). This pattern should be documented in tests/conftest.py so future contributors don't reinvent the wheel with an async fixture that ends up cross-contaminating pytest-asyncio event loops.

rca of the issue: N/A — verification pass. The applied fix is CORRECT and MINIMAL. Root cause of the original blocker: `run_seeds()` was invoked unconditionally from server.py lifespan startup, and its body unconditionally called `_upsert_companies()` + `_upsert_sample_jobs()` + `_ensure_user()` (admin/support/user-zero) + `_rebase_fixture_user()`. On a fresh production Mongo this would have created 4 accounts with hardcoded passwords readable from `domains/seeds/data.py` in the repo + 15 SampleCo demo jobs, a P0 leak. Mitigation applied: an `if settings.PROD_MODE: return counts_with_zeros_plus_flag` short-circuit AFTER taxonomy + feature_flags (both of which are safe reference data with no credentials), plus a mirroring 503 guard on the /api/internal/fixture/rebase escape hatch. Verification strategy: (a) unit tests with monkeypatched `settings.PROD_MODE=True` and an ephemeral db assert both the counts dict and the actual users/jobs/companies collections are empty of the forbidden emails, (b) unit tests with PROD_MODE=False assert the full 15-job + 4-account seed still lands, (c) live preview probe confirms the fixture user still logs in and produces the 9/6 acceptance geometry, (d) subprocess fail-fast probes confirm the two other prod-mode guardrails (CI issuer conflict + empty CORS) still refuse to boot. All layers green.
